To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mitochondrial membrane potential, as measured by the absorbance of entrapped arsenazo-III, is depolarized by veratridine and by FCCP.
in nerve endings the mitochondrial membrane potential controls intracellular free calcium and that this control is mediated via the mitochondrial Na+-Ca2+ exchanger.
the mitochondrial calcium buffering system in synaptosomes plays a significant role in the maintenance of the cytoplasmic calcium concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of calcium-induced calcium release from intracellular organelles, which are involved in the regulation of the cytoplasmic calcium in synaptosome.
the role of mitochondria in the regulation of cytoplasmic calcium concentration in nerve endings.
the mechanisms of calcium homeostasis in nerve endings and the role of calcium in the release of neurotransmitters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increase in cytosolic free Ca2+ induced by depolarization of synaptosomal membrane potential is due to the depolarization of the membrane of mitochondria.

the depolarization of the inner mitochondrial membrane increases cytoplasmic calcium by a direct effect on the mitochondrial membrane potential and by an indirect effect, via the Na(+)-K(+)-ATPase, on the cytoplasmic Na+ level, which in turn affects the Na(+)-Ca2+ exchanger.
the calcium transients induced by depolarization of nerve terminals are not only due to calcium influx through voltage-gated channels but also to the calcium release from mitochondria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the calcium released from the intracellular stores is not sufficient to cause transmitter release and that the calcium entering through the plasma membrane is essential for the transmitter release.

the calcium-induced depolarization of the membrane potential of mitochondria, which is the major intracellular calcium buffer in nerve terminals, causes an increase in cytosolic free Ca2+ and thus facilitates transmitter release.
the depolarization of the mitochondria membrane by FCCP increases the free cytosolic Ca2+ and the release of transmitter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondria are an integral part of the intracellular calcium homeostasis in neurons.
the mitochondria play an important role in calcium homeostasis in nerve endings.
mitochondrial membrane depolarization is an important regulator of intracellular calcium homeostasis in nerve endings.
